judges: one fresh sub-agent per try (model sonnet, the player persona), shown brief.txt and that try's three pictures only
brief:
You are holding the − button of an Ableton Move (a hardware groovebox) that plays a drum-machine web app,
"Orbits". The room is dark and the laptop screen is OFF: all you have is the Move's own lights. Your pattern has 4
lanes and it is playing. The app's manual (its Move table) says:
  −                                  evolve on/off · with ?drift: on the release, for a tap (under 0.45 s) with nothing else pressed, touched or turned while − was down; a longer hold is a look and toggles nothing
  Hold − + knobs 1–8 (with ?drift)   drift: every · amount · gravity · home after · max cycle · coupling lift · humanize · dice repeat · a touched knob turns all 16 step LEDs into its meter (counts light one LED each, percentages in 16ths)
  Hold − + steps (with ?drift)       step LEDs 1–6 = the lanes that evolve (lit in the lane colour; dark = steady), tap one to toggle it · LEDs 9–16 drain toward the next mutation, one per ⅛ of "every" (all dark while evolve is off)
(Evolve mutates the pattern every "every" bars; amount is how much of it a mutation may change.)

Three photos of the Move, each drawn from its lights at that moment. The display is dark, the 8 knobs and the wheel
have no lights, and the 16 step buttons are the row of small lights numbered 1–16 under the pads.
  photo-1.png  − held, no knob touched
  photo-2.png  − held, a finger resting on knob 1 (the leftmost of the 8 knobs), not turning it
  photo-3.png  − held, a finger resting on knob 2, not turning it
Look at these three images only (open them with the Read tool): do not open any other file and do not run anything.
Then answer, as JSON on one line:
{"every": N, "amount": P, "lanes": [..], "lit": L, "bars": B, "notes": "..."}
- every: the "every" setting, in bars
- amount: the "amount" setting, in percent
- lanes: the numbers of the lanes that evolve
- lit: how many of the countdown LEDs (steps 9–16) are lit in photo 1
- bars: roughly how many bars until the next mutation (one number; decimals are fine)
- notes: anything that was hard to read, in a sentence or two. If you cannot tell something, give your best guess.

tries.notes: Lanes are read by LED position (1, 2 and 4 lit; 3 dark). The LED colours don't match the lane colours: LED 2 is cyan, not yellow, and LED 4 is lavender, not white. Every is 8 because photo 2 shows 8 LEDs lit. Amount is 50% because photo 3 shows 8 of 16 LEDs lit. The countdown has 7 of the 8 LEDs lit (9-15, with 16 dark), so about 7 of the 8 bars remain.

Knob 1 lit steps 1-8 (8 bars) and knob 2 lit steps 1-8 (8/16 = 50%). In photo 1, LEDs 1, 2 and 4 are lit and 3 and 5-6 are dark. The LED colours (lilac, cyan, lilac) don't clearly match the lane colours, so the lane numbers come from which LEDs are lit. Countdown LEDs 9-11 are lit (3 of 8), so about 3 bars of an 8-bar cycle remain.

Photo 2 (knob 1) shows 8 step LEDs lit, so every=8 bars. Photo 3 (knob 2) shows 8 lit, so amount=8/16=50%. In photo 1, LEDs 1, 2 and 4 are lit and 3 is dark, so lane 3 is steady. The lit LEDs are pale purple, cyan and lavender rather than clean lane colours, so I could not match them to lanes with certainty. LEDs 9-12 are lit and 13-16 dark. I assumed the lit ones are the time remaining, so 4 of 8 gives about half of 8 bars, roughly 4. If they instead show time already elapsed, the answer is still about 4.

Photo 2 (knob 1) shows 8 of 16 LEDs lit, so every = 8 bars. Photo 3 (knob 2) also shows 8 of 16 lit, so amount = 8/16 = 50%. In photo 1, LEDs 1, 2 and 4 are lit and 3 is dark, so lane 3 is steady. The LED colours (pale purple, cyan, lavender) don't clearly match the lane colours, so the lane numbers are inferred from LED position. Countdown LEDs 9-13 are lit (5 of 8). At 1/8 of every per LED, that is 5/8 of 8 bars, about 5 bars.

Photos 2 and 3 each show 8 of 16 LEDs lit, so every is 8 bars and amount is 8/16 = 50%. In photo 1 the step LEDs have odd colours that don't match the lane colours: 1, 2 and 4 are lit and 3, 5 and 6 are dark. I took LED 3 as the steady lane, but the lane-to-colour mapping is a guess. Steps 9 and 10 are lit, so 2 of 8 countdown LEDs remain, about 2 bars (2/8 of 8). That assumes lit LEDs mean time remaining.
